q.s: A 26-year-old woman takes a drug for severe cystic acne. She becomes pregnant despite counseling. Her baby is born with small malformed ears, a cleft palate, a conotruncal heart defect and a small thymus.
e: Correct. Craniofacial, CNS, cardiac and thymic defects.
q.ch: Acne treatment + microtia + cleft + heart + thymic defects → isotretinoin embryopathy.
q.tr: Two forms of contraception are mandatory.
q.q2: Which drug did she most likely take?

q.s: A woman with a mechanical mitral valve continued her anticoagulant through the first trimester. Her baby has a hypoplastic nose, stippled epiphyses on x-ray and short limbs.
e: Correct. Heparin does not cross the placenta.
q.ch: Warfarin in first trimester → stippled epiphyses, nasal hypoplasia → use heparin in pregnancy.
q.tr: Warfarin also causes optic atrophy and cerebral hemorrhage.
q.q2: Which drug caused these defects, and what should have been used instead?

q.s: A newborn has small eye openings, a smooth area between the nose and upper lip, a thin upper lip and a small head. He has a ventricular septal defect. His mother denies drug use.
o: Impaired migration of neuronal and glial cells from alcohol exposure
cl: a smooth area between the nose and upper lip
q.ch: Small palpebral fissures + smooth philtrum + thin lip + microcephaly + heart defect → fetal alcohol syndrome.
q.tr: A leading preventable cause of intellectual disability.
q.q2: What is a key mechanism of this baby's brain abnormality?

q.s: At 20 weeks, a woman has twins sharing a single placenta. One twin is small with almost no amniotic fluid around it; the other twin is large with excess fluid and an enlarged heart.
cl: almost no amniotic fluid around it
excess fluid and an enlarged heart
q.ch: Shared placenta + separate sacs + donor/recipient → monochorionic diamniotic → split days 4–8 → twin-twin transfusion.
q.tr: "Take separate cars or share a CAB."
q.q2: When did the embryo most likely split?

q.s: A newborn has clear fluid leaking from his umbilicus. The fluid has a high urea and creatinine concentration. He has no other anomalies.
cl: clear fluid leaking from his umbilicus
q.ch: Urine from the umbilicus → patent urachus (allantois remnant from bladder to umbilicus).
q.tr: Its obliterated remnant is the median umbilical ligament.
q.q2: Which structure failed to obliterate?

q.s: A 7-year-old boy has a soft, painless lump on the side of his neck just in front of the sternocleidomastoid. It does not move when he swallows or sticks out his tongue. It became red and tender during a cold.
o: A persistent cervical sinus from the 2nd–4th pharyngeal clefts
cl: on the side of his neck just in front of the sternocleidomastoid
does not move when he swallows
became red and tender during a cold
q.ch: Lateral neck mass anterior to SCM, not moving with swallowing → persistent cervical sinus → pharyngeal cleft cyst.
q.tr: The 1st cleft forms the external auditory meatus.
q.q2: What is the embryologic origin?

q.s: A newborn has seizures on day 2 with a calcium of 6.1 mg/dL. Chest x-ray shows no thymic shadow, and echocardiography shows truncus arteriosus. Over the next year she has repeated viral and fungal infections.
q.ch: Hypocalcemia + absent thymus + conotruncal defect → 3rd/4th pouch failure → DiGeorge (22q11.2 deletion).
q.tr: 3rd pouch forms thymus and inferior parathyroids; 4th forms superior parathyroids.
q.q2: Failure of which structures explains her findings?

q.s: A 16-year-old who has been raised as a girl comes in because she has never had a period. She has a short, blind-ending vagina. Her results are shown.
o: Failure of the paramesonephric ducts from unknown cause
Excess testosterone acting on Müllerian ducts
cl: Distal vagina only from urogenital sinus.
q.ch: 46,XY + breasts + scant hair + no uterus + high testosterone and LH → androgen receptor defect; Sertoli AMH removes Müllerian structures.
q.tr: Gonads are removed to prevent malignancy.
q.q2: Why is the uterus absent?

q.s: A 12-year-old child raised as a girl develops a deeper voice, muscle growth and enlargement of the clitoris into a phallus at puberty. Karyotype is 46,XY. Testosterone and estrogen levels are normal for a male. There is no uterus.
e: Correct. Cannot convert testosterone to DHT.
cl: enlargement of the clitoris into a phallus
q.ch: 46,XY + atypical genitalia at birth + virilization at puberty + normal testosterone → 5α-reductase deficiency.
q.tr: Autosomal recessive and sex-limited to genetic males.
q.q2: Which enzyme is deficient?
q.fc: Family pedigree; shaded individuals are phenotypic females with a 46,XY karyotype, and carriers are marked with a dot

q.s: The 15-year-old proband, who appears female and has a 46,XY karyotype, is shown in the pedigree. Her maternal aunt has the same condition. Her mother and grandmother are carriers.
e: Correct. Androgen insensitivity syndrome (AR gene on X).
cl: appears female and has a 46,XY karyotype
Her maternal aunt has the same condition
Her mother and grandmother are carriers
q.ch: Affected 46,XY individuals related through carrier females → X-linked recessive androgen receptor defect.
q.tr: 5α-reductase deficiency is autosomal recessive.
q.q2: What is the inheritance pattern of this condition?

q.s: A 17-year-old boy has not started puberty. He has a small penis and testes and cannot smell perfume. LH, FSH and testosterone are all low. MRI shows absent olfactory bulbs.
o: Failure of GnRH neurons to migrate from the olfactory placode to the hypothalamus
e: Wrong. LH and FSH would be high.
cl: LH, FSH and testosterone are all low
q.ch: Delayed puberty + anosmia + low GnRH/LH/FSH → Kallmann syndrome.
q.tr: Treat with pulsatile GnRH or gonadotropins for fertility.
q.q2: What is the mechanism?

q.s: A 24-year-old man has been trying to conceive for 2 years. He has chronic sinusitis and recurrent pneumonia. Chest x-ray shows his heart on the right side. His semen analysis is shown; almost none of the sperm move.
o: Defective dynein arms in cilia and sperm flagella
Congenital absence of the vas deferens
cl: almost none of the sperm move
q.ch: Situs inversus + sinusitis + bronchiectasis + immotile sperm → primary ciliary dyskinesia (Kartagener).
q.tr: In cystic fibrosis sperm move normally but the vas deferens is absent.
q.q2: Which defect is responsible?
q.fc: Hormone levels during a normal 28-day menstrual cycle

q.s: A medical student studies the hormone curves of a normal menstrual cycle, shown. She notes that estradiol usually inhibits LH secretion.
o: Sustained high estradiol switches to positive feedback on the hypothalamus and pituitary
cl: A medical student studies the hormone curves
q.ch: Rising estradiol from the dominant follicle → positive feedback at midcycle → LH surge → ovulation; progesterone then rises from the corpus luteum.
q.tr: The luteal phase is fixed at 14 days.
q.q2: What explains the sharp LH peak on about day 13?

q.s: A 32-year-old woman has a 21-day menstrual cycle that is regular. She wants to time intercourse to conceive.
e: Correct. Luteal phase is fixed at 14 days.
q.ch: Cycle length − 14 days (fixed luteal phase) = day of ovulation → day 7.
q.tr: Follicular phase length varies; luteal phase does not.
q.q2: On which day does she most likely ovulate?

q.s: A 29-year-old woman with a history of pelvic inflammatory disease has 6 weeks of amenorrhea and spotting with left lower abdominal pain. Her β-hCG levels are shown. Transvaginal ultrasound shows an empty uterus and a left adnexal mass.
e: Wrong. Highest rupture risk but less common.
cl: an empty uterus and a left adnexal mass
q.ch: PID + slow hCG rise + empty uterus + adnexal mass → tubal ectopic (ampulla most common).
q.tr: Treat with methotrexate if stable, surgery if ruptured.
q.q2: Where is this pregnancy most likely implanted?

q.s: A 41-year-old woman with two prior cesarean deliveries and placenta previa delivers by cesarean. The placenta will not separate, and when the surgeon tries to remove it, bleeding is torrential. Pathology shows villi in direct contact with myometrium without decidua.
cl: villi in direct contact with myometrium without decidua
q.ch: Prior cesareans + previa + adherent placenta + hemorrhage → placenta accreta spectrum → hysterectomy.
q.tr: Percreta can invade the bladder and cause hematuria.
q.q2: What is the diagnosis and usual treatment?

q.s: A 35-year-old woman at 34 weeks who smokes and has chronic hypertension has sudden severe abdominal pain and dark red vaginal bleeding. Her uterus is hard and tender. The fetal heart rate shows late decelerations. An hour later blood oozes from her IV sites and fibrinogen is very low.
o: Release of tissue factor from the injured placenta causing DIC
cl: sudden severe abdominal pain and dark red vaginal bleeding
Her uterus is hard and tender
q.ch: Painful third-trimester bleeding + tender uterus + fetal distress → abruption → tissue factor → DIC.
q.tr: Placenta previa causes painless bleeding.
q.q2: What is the mechanism of her bleeding from IV sites?

q.s: Immediately after a vaginal delivery of a 4.3-kg baby after a long labor, a woman loses 1200 mL of blood. Her uterus is soft and boggy and rises above the umbilicus. The placenta was delivered complete, and there are no lacerations.
cl: a 4.3-kg baby after a long labor
Her uterus is soft and boggy
placenta was delivered complete, and there are no lacerations
q.ch: Boggy uterus after delivery + no retained tissue or laceration → uterine atony (tone) → massage + oxytocin.
q.tr: 4 T's: Tone, Trauma, Tissue, Thrombin.
q.q2: What is the first-line treatment?
q.fc: Findings in two patients with gestational trophoblastic disease

q.s: Two women have abnormal pregnancies at 12 weeks with vaginal bleeding. Their findings are shown.
o: Paternal DNA only, from one sperm fertilizing an empty egg and duplicating
Two sperm and one normal egg
q.ch: Complete mole: 46,XX, entirely paternal (p57 negative), no fetus, very high hCG; partial mole: triploid, fetal parts, p57 positive.
q.tr: Complete moles carry a 2% risk of choriocarcinoma.
q.q2: What is the origin of patient 1's genetic material?

q.s: Eight months after evacuation of a complete mole, a 28-year-old woman has shortness of breath and coughs up blood. Her β-hCG, which had normalized, is now 85,000 mIU/mL. Chest x-ray shows multiple round lung masses.
cl: which had normalized, is now 85,000 mIU/mL
q.ch: Prior mole + rising hCG + cannonball lung lesions → choriocarcinoma → methotrexate.
q.tr: Choriocarcinoma has trophoblasts but no villi.
q.q2: What is the most appropriate treatment?

q.s: A 30-year-old woman at 35 weeks has severe right upper quadrant pain, nausea and malaise. Her results are shown.
q.ch: Hemolysis (schistocytes, high LDH) + elevated liver enzymes + low platelets in late pregnancy → HELLP → deliver.
q.tr: Risk of hepatic subcapsular hematoma rupture and DIC.
q.q2: What is the definitive treatment?

q.s: A 22-year-old woman at 37 weeks has a headache and BP of 168/112 mm Hg. Urine protein is 3+. While being examined she has a generalized tonic-clonic seizure.
e: Wrong. Not the drug of choice.
q.ch: Preeclampsia + seizure → eclampsia → IV magnesium sulfate + antihypertensives + delivery.
q.tr: Watch for magnesium toxicity: lost reflexes, respiratory depression.
q.q2: Which drug should be given immediately?

q.s: A 26-year-old woman has irregular periods every 2–3 months, acne and coarse hair on her chin. Her BMI is 33. She has dark, velvety skin in her armpits. Ultrasound shows enlarged ovaries with many peripheral follicles.
o: Endometrial hyperplasia and carcinoma from unopposed estrogen
cl: dark, velvety skin in her armpits
q.ch: Oligo-ovulation + hyperandrogenism + polycystic ovaries → PCOS → no progesterone → endometrial hyperplasia/cancer.
q.tr: OCPs protect the endometrium.
q.q2: Which long-term risk is increased because of her irregular ovulation?

q.s: A 20-year-old college runner has not menstruated for 7 months. Her BMI is 17.2. She recently had a stress fracture of her foot. Pregnancy test is negative. LH, FSH and estradiol are low; prolactin and TSH are normal.
o: Low leptin and high cortisol suppress pulsatile GnRH secretion
e: Wrong. Estrogen normal in that case.
cl: LH, FSH and estradiol are low
q.ch: Low energy availability + amenorrhea + bone loss → female athlete triad → ↓ GnRH pulsatility.
q.tr: Treat by restoring energy balance.
q.q2: What is the mechanism of her amenorrhea?

q.s: A 31-year-old woman has an abnormal Pap test. Colposcopic biopsy shows cells with wrinkled nuclei and perinuclear clearing, and dysplasia involving the full thickness of the epithelium without invasion.
cl: full thickness of the epithelium without invasion
q.ch: Koilocytes + full-thickness dysplasia → high-risk HPV (16, 18) → E6 degrades p53, E7 binds pRb.
q.tr: "6 before 7; P before R."
q.q2: Which viral protein inactivates p53 in these cells?

q.s: A 23-year-old woman has sudden severe left pelvic pain and vomiting while playing volleyball. Ultrasound shows a 7-cm left ovarian cyst and absent venous flow in the left ovary.
cl: sudden severe left pelvic pain and vomiting
q.ch: Ovarian mass → twisting around the infundibulopelvic and ovarian ligaments → venous then arterial obstruction → necrosis → surgical emergency.
q.tr: Ligating the infundibulopelvic ligament risks injuring the ureter.
q.q2: Twisting around which ligament compresses the ovarian vessels?
q.fc: Tumor markers and histology in three patients with ovarian masses

q.s: Three girls and women have solid ovarian masses. Their findings are shown.
o: Granulosa cell tumor; postmenopausal bleeding from estrogen
q.ch: Fried-egg cells + hCG/LDH → dysgerminoma; Schiller-Duval + AFP → yolk sac tumor; Call-Exner + inhibin → granulosa cell tumor (estrogen → bleeding).
q.tr: "Give Granny a Call."
q.q2: Which tumor does patient 3 have, and what symptom is she likely to have?

q.s: A 52-year-old woman has a pulling sensation in her groin, shortness of breath and abdominal swelling. Imaging shows a solid left ovarian mass, ascites and a right pleural effusion. All resolve after the mass is removed.
cl: ascites and a right pleural effusion
All resolve after the mass is removed
q.ch: Ovarian mass + ascites + pleural effusion resolving with resection → Meigs syndrome → fibroma.
q.tr: Fibromas are benign sex cord stromal tumors.
q.q2: What is the histology of the mass?

q.s: A 45-year-old woman has heavy, painful periods. Her uterus is uniformly enlarged to the size of a 10-week pregnancy and is soft and tender on exam. Pregnancy test is negative.
o: Endometrial glands and stroma within the myometrium
q.ch: AUB + dysmenorrhea + diffusely enlarged boggy uterus → adenomyosis.
q.tr: Leiomyomas give a firm, nodular uterus.
q.q2: What is the histologic finding in her uterus?

q.s: A 29-year-old woman has painful periods, deep pain with intercourse and has been unable to conceive for 2 years. Pelvic exam shows tender nodules along the uterosacral ligaments. Laparoscopy shows dark brown cysts on both ovaries.
o: Invagination of the basalis into myometrium
Retrograde menstruation implanting endometrial tissue outside the uterus
cl: tender nodules along the uterosacral ligaments
dark brown cysts on both ovaries
q.ch: Dysmenorrhea + dyspareunia + infertility + chocolate cysts → endometriosis.
q.tr: Peritoneal implants look like "powder burns."
q.q2: Which is a proposed mechanism of her disease?

q.s: A 61-year-old obese woman who never had children has new vaginal bleeding 9 years after menopause. She took estrogen without progesterone for 6 years. Biopsy shows back-to-back glands with no intervening stroma.
cl: obese woman who never had children
back-to-back glands with no intervening stroma
q.ch: Unopposed estrogen + obesity + nulliparity + postmenopausal bleeding → endometrioid carcinoma.
q.tr: Most common gynecologic cancer in resource-rich countries.
q.q2: What is the most likely diagnosis?

q.s: A 58-year-old woman has a hard, fixed lump in the upper outer quadrant of her left breast with dimpling of the overlying skin. Biopsy shows cells arranged in single-file lines with no duct formation.
cl: single-file lines with no duct formation
q.ch: Breast mass + single-file cells without ducts → invasive lobular carcinoma → loss of E-cadherin.
q.tr: Often bilateral and multifocal.
q.q2: Loss of which protein explains this growth pattern?

q.s: A 15-year-old boy has sudden severe right scrotal pain that woke him from sleep, with nausea and vomiting. The right testis lies high and horizontal. The cremasteric reflex is absent on the right, and lifting the scrotum does not relieve pain.
o: Immediate surgical exploration with bilateral orchiopexy
cl: sudden severe right scrotal pain that woke him from sleep
lifting the scrotum does not relieve pain
q.ch: Acute scrotal pain + high horizontal testis + absent cremasteric reflex + negative Prehn → torsion → surgery within 6 hours.
q.tr: Fix both testes.
q.q2: What is the most appropriate next step?

q.s: A 31-year-old man has a painless, heavy, enlarged left testis. Ultrasound shows a homogeneous solid mass. Serum AFP is normal and β-hCG is slightly elevated. Placental alkaline phosphatase is high.
o: It secretes androgens causing precocious puberty
It is the most common testicular tumor in children under 3
It should be biopsied through the scrotum
It metastasizes early to lungs and brain
It is highly radiosensitive with an excellent prognosis
q.ch: Young man + homogeneous painless testis mass + normal AFP + high PLAP → seminoma → radiosensitive, good prognosis.
q.tr: Elevated AFP rules out a pure seminoma.
q.q2: Which statement about this tumor is correct?

q.s: A 72-year-old man has urinary frequency, nocturia and a weak stream. Rectal exam shows a smooth, rubbery, symmetrically enlarged prostate. He wants a drug that will shrink the prostate over months and also reduce his risk of urinary retention.
e: Wrong. Relaxes smooth muscle, does not shrink.
cl: urinary frequency, nocturia and a weak stream
q.ch: BPH + desire to shrink gland → finasteride (↓ DHT); tamsulosin gives rapid symptom relief.
q.tr: Finasteride lowers PSA by about half.
q.q2: Which drug fits?

q.s: A 70-year-old man has had 3 months of worsening low back pain. Rectal exam shows a hard, nodular prostate. Serum PSA is 94 ng/mL with a low free-PSA fraction, and alkaline phosphatase is elevated. Bone scan shows multiple lesions in the lumbar spine.
q.ch: Prostate adenocarcinoma → Batson vertebral venous plexus → osteoblastic spinal metastases.
q.tr: Graded with the Gleason system.
q.q2: Through which pathway did the tumor most likely reach the spine?

q.s: A 64-year-old man with metastatic prostate cancer starts leuprolide. Two weeks later he has worsening bone pain and new difficulty urinating. His physician adds a second drug.
cl: worsening bone pain and new difficulty urinating
q.ch: Continuous GnRH agonist → initial LH and testosterone surge → flare → prevent with androgen receptor blocker (flutamide) or use degarelix.
q.tr: Degarelix is a GnRH antagonist without flare.
q.q2: Which drug should have been started with leuprolide to prevent this, and how does it work?

q.s: A 54-year-old woman has taken tamoxifen for 3 years after surgery for ER-positive breast cancer. She now has vaginal spotting. Ultrasound shows a thickened endometrium.
o: It is an antagonist at the endometrium
It is a partial estrogen agonist at the uterus, causing hyperplasia or carcinoma
q.ch: Tamoxifen: antagonist in breast, partial agonist in uterus and bone → endometrial hyperplasia/cancer.
q.tr: Raloxifene does not stimulate the endometrium.
q.q2: Why does tamoxifen cause this?

q.s: A 28-year-old woman with PCOS who has not ovulated for a year wants to become pregnant. Her physician prescribes a drug that blocks estrogen receptors in the hypothalamus. Three weeks later she has hot flashes and blurred vision.
o: It blocks estrogen negative feedback, increasing GnRH, LH and FSH
It blocks aromatase in the ovary
cl: has not ovulated for a year
blocks estrogen receptors in the hypothalamus
q.ch: Clomiphene blocks hypothalamic estrogen feedback → ↑ GnRH → ↑ LH/FSH → ovulation; risk of multiple pregnancy and visual changes.
q.tr: Letrozole is an alternative.
q.q2: How does the drug induce ovulation?

q.s: A 36-year-old woman at 31 weeks has regular painful contractions every 4 minutes and her cervix is dilating. Her physician gives a drug to slow contractions and an intramuscular steroid for the baby.
q.ch: Preterm labor → tocolysis buys time → antenatal glucocorticoids accelerate surfactant production.
q.tr: "Keep the baby in the TIN."
q.q2: Why is the steroid given?
